info.title: Tucano Test API
info.description: File-based test case management API. Data is stored as JSON files; no database is used.

get.summary: Read a project, assembling the suites and directly owned cases it holds

delete.summary: Delete a project and everything below it

get.summary: List the test suites a project owns

post.summary: Create a test suite in a project, or place an existing one
post.description: A body with a non-empty `name` creates a suite, identified as `<name>.json`. Otherwise the body names an existing `suiteId` to place here, and `mode` chooses copy (the default) or move.

delete.summary: Delete a test suite a project owns

get.summary: List the test cases a project directly owns

post.summary: Create a test case in a project, or place an existing one
post.description: A body carrying a `title` creates a case and must also carry the `testCaseId` and `expectedResult` a case needs. Otherwise the body names an existing `testCaseId` to place here, and `mode` chooses copy (the default) or move.

delete.summary: Delete a test case a project owns

get.summary: Read a test suite with the cases it holds assembled

delete.summary: Delete a test suite and the cases it holds

get.summary: List the test cases a suite holds

post.summary: Create a test case in a suite, or place an existing one
post.description: A body carrying a `title` creates a case in the suite and must also carry the `testCaseId` and `expectedResult` a case needs. Otherwise the body names an existing `testCaseId` to place here, and `mode` chooses copy (the default) or move.

delete.summary: Remove a test case from a suite

get.description: A run is a point-in-time snapshot. `filter` and `tags` behave as they do elsewhere; `configuration` is meaningful here alone and keeps the runs that link the given configuration, so a configuration no run links yields an empty listing.

post.description: A run is a point-in-time snapshot, never a home: the suite is recorded as a copy and keeps the project that owns it, so this does not relocate the source. An unusable path identifier or `suiteId` answers `invalid_id`.

A run is a point-in-time snapshot, never a home: the case is recorded as a copy and keeps the project or suite that owns it, so this does not relocate the source. An unusable path identifier answers `invalid_id`.

post.summary: Record test case execution result in run

get.summary: List the defects linked to a run result
get.description: Returns the defect links recorded on the result a run holds for `case_id`. An unusable run identifier answers `invalid_id`, and a run that does not exist or records no result for that case answers `404`, so an empty list means the result exists but has no linked defect.

200.description: Defect links recorded on one run result

post.summary: Link a defect to a run result
post.description: Records a defect link on the result a run holds for `case_id`. The API derives the link identifier and the linked-at timestamp, so a body carrying either is rejected rather than silently ignored. `defectUrl` must be an issue URL the named `trackerType` would use: `jira` a `<org>.atlassian.net/browse/<KEY>` URL, `github` a `github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<number>` URL, `gitlab` a `gitlab.com/<group>/<project>/-/issues/<number>` URL, and `custom` any well-formed `https://` URL. A `defectId` the result already links answers `409` rather than adding a second link.

id.description: Identifier the API assigned to the new link; pass it to the unlink route.

delete.summary: Unlink a defect from a run result
delete.description: Removes the defect link a result carries under `link_id`. The identifier is the one the link route returned and is an opaque string, not a stored document name, so it is not validated as one. An unknown run or result, or a result that does not carry that link, answers `404`.

post.summary: Import JUnit XML results into a run
post.description: Reads a JUnit XML report and records a result for every `<testcase>` it can name at any depth, mapping a failure or error to `Failed`, a skip to `Blocked` and anything else to `Passed`. A case the run already records is counted as a duplicate and left untouched, and a case carrying no `name` is counted as an error, so a partly unusable report still imports the part that is not. The body must be UTF-8 and well-formed XML; anything else answers `invalid_request`.

post.summary: Import JSON results into a run
post.description: Reads a JSON array of results — or an object whose only field `results` holds that array — and records one result per entry, each becoming the same `TestCaseResult` the single-result route writes. An entry's `timestamp` is stored verbatim and defaults to the current time; `notes` is optional. The body is strict: malformed JSON, an entry that is not an object, an unknown or misspelled field, a missing or empty `testCaseId` or `status`, or a `status` that is not `Passed`, `Failed` or `Blocked` answers `invalid_request` (or `invalid_status`) and nothing is written, because the whole body is parsed before the run is touched. A case the run already records is counted as a duplicate and left untouched.

post.summary: Link a configuration to a run
post.description: A run references the top-level configuration instead of embedding a copy of it, so the link records the configuration's identifier and name. An unusable run or `configId` answers `invalid_id`, an unknown one answers `404`, and linking a configuration the run already references answers `409`.

delete.summary: Unlink a configuration from a run
delete.description: Removes the run's reference to the configuration. An unusable run identifier answers `invalid_id`, and a configuration the run does not reference answers `404`.

get.description: A bare identifier that several parents hold is a conflict; address the case through its parent-scoped route instead. Test case identifiers are addressed verbatim, so an unusable one is a `404` and never an `invalid_id`.

put.description: Test case identifiers are addressed verbatim, so an unusable one is a `404` and never an `invalid_id`. A change to `title`, `steps`, `preconditions` or `expectedResult` records an immutable `revisions/v{version}.json` snapshot of the previous document and starts a new version; any other update leaves `version` and `lastModified` untouched. `version` and `lastModified` are always API-managed, so a value the body supplies is ignored.

delete.description: A bare identifier that several parents hold is a conflict; address the case through its parent-scoped route instead. Test case identifiers are addressed verbatim, so an unusable one is a `404` and never an `invalid_id`.

post.description: The first multipart part is the attachment; its part name is not inspected, but it must carry a filename. A bare identifier that several parents hold is a conflict; address the case through its parent-scoped route instead.

get.description: A bare identifier that several parents hold is a conflict; address the case through its parent-scoped route instead.

delete.description: A bare identifier that several parents hold is a conflict; address the case through its parent-scoped route instead.

get.description: Returns the metadata recorded for the addressed structured step, an empty array when it carries none. The index walks the case's `steps` array, where a plain string step has no attachments. A bare identifier that several parents hold is a conflict, and a case addressed by an unusable identifier answers `404`, never `400`.

post.description: The first multipart part is the attachment; its part name is not inspected, but it must carry a filename. The metadata is appended to the addressed structured step. A bare identifier that several parents hold is a conflict, and a case addressed by an unusable identifier answers `404`, never `400`.

delete.description: Removes the file and its metadata. An unattached filename answers `404`. A bare identifier that several parents hold is a conflict, and a case addressed by an unusable identifier answers `404`, never `400`.

get.description: The case's recorded snapshots, oldest first. The current live version is not a snapshot and is not listed, and a case that has never had a qualifying update lists as an empty array. The case is resolved before anything else, so an unknown case is a `404`. A bare identifier that several parents hold is a conflict; test case identifiers are addressed verbatim, so an unusable one is a `404` and never an `invalid_id`.

Returns the immutable snapshot recorded at `version`. A version the case never recorded answers `404`, and so does the current live version, which is read through `GET /test_cases/{id}`. The case is resolved before the version is parsed, so an unknown case answers `404` even when the version is unusable. A bare identifier that several parents hold is a conflict; test case identifiers are addressed verbatim, so an unusable one is a `404` and never an `invalid_id`.

post.description: An unusable path identifier answers `invalid_request` here, where `POST /test_suites/{id}/duplicate` answers `invalid_id`. Unknown fields in the body are ignored.
An unusable path identifier answers `invalid_id` here, where the project, run, milestone and case duplicate routes answer `invalid_request`. Unknown fields in the body are ignored.
Unknown fields in the body are ignored.

post.summary: Duplicate test run without its results
post.description: Unknown fields in the body are ignored.

The copy keeps the source's name, dates, status and referenced suites and runs, so it reports the same derived progress; editing or deleting either milestone leaves the other intact. Unknown fields in the body are ignored.

newId.description: Identifier for the copy; derived from the source when omitted

step_index.name: step_index

schema.description: 0-based index of the step inside the case's `steps` array

step_index.description: A value that is not a non-negative integer is reported as `invalid_request`.

version.name: version

schema.description: Revision number of the snapshot, as listed by `GET /test_cases/{id}/history`

version.description: A value that is not a positive integer is reported as `invalid_request`.

link_id.name: link_id
link_id.description: Identifier of a defect link, as returned by the route that recorded it. It is an opaque string the API derives, not a stored document name, so it is never validated as one.

filter.name: filter
filter.description: Case-insensitive substring filter for resource IDs

tags.name: tags
tags.description: Comma-separated tags; a resource matches when it carries at least one of them (case-insensitive). Resources without a tags array never match.

configuration.name: configuration
configuration.description: Only meaningful for test_runs: keeps the runs that link the given configuration identifier. A configuration no run links yields an empty listing.

TestRun.description: A point-in-time snapshot of the suites, cases and results a run recorded. The snapshot embeds a copy of each referenced document, so a later edit to the source leaves the run unchanged.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds rendered as a string, as written by this API; a client-supplied value is stored verbatim, so the field is not necessarily an ISO-8601 date.

caseVersions.description: The revision of each case the run pinned when the case was added or its result recorded, keyed by the case identifier (`testCaseId`). The run never re-reads a case, so a later qualifying edit leaves these values unchanged; the first capture wins, and a case that carries no `version` of its own is pinned as `1`.

newId.description: Identifier for the copy; derived from the source when omitted

newName.description: Name for the copy; the source name is kept when omitted

newId.description: Identifier for the copy; derived from the source when omitted

newTitle.description: Title for the copy; the source title is kept when omitted

newId.description: Identifier for the copy; derived from the source when omitted

AttachmentUpload.description: The first multipart part is the attachment. Its part name is not inspected, so any name works, but the part must carry a filename; a part without one is reported as `missing_file`.

file.description: Conventional part name; the handler accepts any.

StepAttachment.description: Metadata of a file attached to one structured step. Unlike `Attachment` it carries no `uploadedAt`.

version.description: The case's current revision number; the API stamps 1 when it creates the case and increments it on every qualifying update. A client-supplied value is ignored.

lastModified.description: When the current version was written, in ISO-8601 UTC. The API stamps it on creation and on every qualifying update; a client-supplied value is ignored.

TestResultRequest.description: The execution result recorded for one case in a run. Unknown fields are ignored, and a `timestamp` supplied by the client is stored verbatim.

timestamp.description: Defaults to the current time in Unix seconds, rendered as a string

ImportSummary.description: What one JUnit import did. `skipped` is the cases deliberately left unwritten: the `duplicates` the run already recorded plus the `errors` it could not map, so `imported + skipped` is every `<testcase>` the report held.

errors.description: Cases that could not be named and were not written

duplicates.description: Cases the run already recorded, left untouched

ImportCounts.description: How the imported results split by the status they were mapped to, so `passed + failed + blocked` is the import's `imported` count.

ImportEntry.description: One result of a JSON import. Only `Passed`, `Failed` and `Blocked` are accepted — the three outcomes a runner reports — so `Untested` and `Retest` are rejected as `invalid_status`.

testCaseId.description: The case the result belongs to; required and must not be empty.

timestamp.description: Stored verbatim; the current time in Unix seconds when omitted.

DefectLink.description: A reference from a run result to the defect a failure raised. `trackerType` names the system the defect lives in — `jira`, `github`, `gitlab` or `custom` — and `defectUrl` is the address a human follows to reach it. `linkId` is the link's own identity, so the same defect can be linked and unlinked without depending on its position in the list.

linkId.description: The link's own identity, independent of the defect it names

defectId.description: The defect's identifier inside its tracker

defectUrl.description: Where the defect can be read

linkedAt.description: Unix seconds rendered as a string, or a value stored verbatim.

DefectLinkRequest.description: The client-supplied half of a defect link. The API derives `linkId` and `linkedAt`, so a body that carries either — or any other unknown field — is rejected rather than silently ignored: a client that thought it was naming the link would otherwise never learn its identifier was thrown away. `defectUrl` must be an issue URL the named `trackerType` would use, and `trackerType` must be one of the four the API knows.

defectId.description: The defect's identifier inside its tracker; a result may link a given `defectId` only once.

defectUrl.description: An issue URL for `trackerType`: a `<org>.atlassian.net/browse/<KEY>` URL for `jira`, a `github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<number>` URL for `github`, a `gitlab.com/<group>/<project>/-/issues/<number>` URL for `gitlab`, and any well-formed `https://` URL for `custom`. A query string or fragment is ignored.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds rendered as a string, as written by this API; a client-supplied value is stored verbatim, so the field is not necessarily an ISO-8601 date.

CaseHistoryEntry.description: One recorded revision of a case. `changedFields` lists the qualifying fields — `title`, `steps`, `preconditions`, `expectedResult` — in which the snapshot differs from the version that superseded it, so the newest snapshot's entry compares against the live document. `lastModified` is the snapshot's own stamp, absent for a snapshot written before versioning, which is why it is not required.

TestSuite.description: A test suite document. The stored marker keeps `testCases` empty; reads fill it with the cases the suite folder holds.

Project.description: A project document. Reads replace `testSuites` with the suites the project holds (each carrying its cases) and add `testCases` for the cases held directly — a response-only field, omitted when the project owns no case directly.

CompositionRequest.description: Creation-or-placement body shared by the parent-scoped collection routes. A body with `name` (suite) or `title` (case) creates: the new suite is identified as `<name>.json`, the new case by its `testCaseId`, and `expectedResult` is required alongside a case `title`. Otherwise the body names an existing `suiteId`/`testCaseId` to place that child here, with `mode` choosing copy (the default) or move. `mode` alongside the fields that create is a 400, as is a `mode` other than `copy` or `move`. Fields the reading in use does not know are ignored, so the schema does not claim `additionalProperties: false`.

name.description: Creation: the suite name; the identifier is always `<name>.json`

suiteId.description: Placement: the existing suite to copy or move here. Ignored when the body creates.

testCaseId.description: Creation: the identifier of the new case. Placement: the existing case to copy or move here

expectedResult.description: Creation: the result the case expects; required alongside `title`

mode.description: Placement only: `copy` duplicates the child into this parent and keeps the source in place (the default); `move` relocates it

InvalidId.description: `invalid_id`: an identifier must be a single path component ending in `.json`. Test cases are addressed verbatim and answer `404` instead, and the duplicate routes differ as their own descriptions record.

InvalidRequest.description: `invalid_request`: the body was rejected — an unknown or missing field, an identifier the body supplies that is not a single `.json` component, or a name-only payload that omits what creation needs.

InvalidIdOrRequest.description: `invalid_id` for an identifier in the path or the body that is not a single `.json` component, or `invalid_request` for a rejected body.

InvalidIdOrRequestOrStatus.description: `invalid_id` for an unusable identifier, `invalid_request` for a missing or rejected field, or `invalid_status` when `status` is not `Passed`, `Failed`, `Blocked`, `Untested` or `Retest`.

InvalidIdOrRequestOrImportStatus.description: `invalid_id` for an unusable identifier, `invalid_request` for a body that is not a JSON results array or an entry that is not an object, omits or misspells a field, or supplies an empty `testCaseId`, or `invalid_status` when an entry's `status` is not `Passed`, `Failed` or `Blocked`.

AttachmentRejected.description: The upload route's 400s. `invalid_multipart` when the multipart body cannot be parsed and `missing_file` when no part carries a filename, both as the error envelope; but the multipart extractor rejects a request that is not valid `multipart/form-data` before the handler runs, and that answer is plain text — `Invalid \`boundary\` for \`multipart/form-data\` request` — not the envelope.

InvalidStepIndex.description: `invalid_request`: the step index is not a non-negative integer, is beyond the end of the case's `steps` array, or names a plain string step rather than a structured one.

InvalidVersion.description: `invalid_request`: the revision number is not a positive integer.

StepAttachmentRejected.description: The step upload route's 400s. `invalid_request` when the step index is unusable, `invalid_multipart` when the multipart body cannot be parsed and `missing_file` when no part carries a filename, all as the error envelope; but the multipart extractor rejects a request that is not valid `multipart/form-data` before the handler runs, and that answer is plain text.

BodyTooLarge.description: Every request is capped at 50 MiB by the router, before the handler runs: the answer is plain text — `length limit exceeded` — never the error envelope. Because the router cap and the attachment cap are the same size, the `payload_too_large` envelope the API can still produce is unreachable for attachments, and this plain-text 413 is the only observable one.
